Neonatal Training Weaning Resources Neonatal Training Neonatal Kitten Online Training The following training through Maddie's Fund is a fantastic resource for anyone fostering neonatal kittens, whether it’s a first-time experience or just a refresher before kitten season ramps up. The interactive format allows fosters to move through topics at their own pace and focus on the areas where they want additional guidance or support. Topics covered include: Preparing for the arrival of neonatal kittens Monitoring kitten health and recognizing concerns early Setting up safe, age-appropriate housing Bottle feeding and syringe feeding techniques Stimulating kittens to eliminate Weaning kittens onto solid food Bathing kittens safely Socializing kittens and supporting healthy development Neonatal kittens can be tiny, fragile, and very dramatic about mealtime schedules, but trainings like this can help fosters feel much more confident and prepared. Find this informative and FREE training here. Weaning Weaning A big part of fostering kittens is the weaning process, which includes knowing when to wean and how to wean. Kitten Lady has a page on her website that helps walk you through when a kitten is ready to wean, what is needed and how to do it. Kitten Soup Ingredients: ½ Can wet kitten food 1 Full scoop KMR (Kitten Milk Replacer) 2-3 Tablespoon(s) of water Instructions: 1) Put ½ can wet kitten food and 1 scoop KMR (there should be a clear scoop in the KMR container) into wet food bowl. 2) MIX THE WET FOOD AND KMR TOGETHER WITHOUT ADDING WATER until there are no more lumps of KMR and everything is combined. 3) Add water slowly stirring as you add water until the mixture is the texture of applesauce (can add more or less water to suit the preference of the individual animal, also use warm water if the wet food has been in the refrigerator). This makes one serving and should be multiplied to serve the number of animals in need. Kitten Lady has videos and articles about preparing for fosters, supplies, caring for kittens, and more. Maddie's University has a lot of great classes, including this free "Taking the Fear out of Bottle Feeding and Basic Kitten Care" class that walks the taker through bottle feeding and basic kitten care.

Website Sign In Home Government Departments A - F Animal Services Get Involved Dog Adventures Hikes with Hounds Hikes with Hounds Hikes with Hounds is a monthly enrichment program hosted by Orange County Animal Services in partnership with Orange County Department of Environment, Agriculture, Parks and Recreation. Inspired by the success of Hikes with Hounds in Alamance County , this initiative gives adoptable dogs the opportunity to step out of the kennel environment and onto the trail for a couple of hours of fresh air, exercise, and positive social interaction. Our goal is to schedule these hikes monthly at Blackwood Farm Park , the program pairs pre-registered volunteers with selected dogs for a guided group hike. Participants meet in the park’s parking lot before heading out together to explore the trails during a 3-mile hike . This hike is generally considered easy to the very low-end of moderate, but it may feel more strenuous in extreme temperatures. Also, these dogs are energetic and happy to be outdoors, meaning you'll likely be walking a playful companion that does some pulling due to excitement. So, please hydrate and prepare to get your exercise! Hikes with Hounds is designed to: Provide mental and physical enrichment for adoptable dogs Offer volunteers a meaningful, hands-on experience outside of the facility Increase community engagement and visibility for dogs looking for homes Support positive leash skills, confidence building, and socialization Participation is limited to ensure a safe and structured experience for both people and dogs. Advance registration is required, and hikers are capped each month. By combining outdoor recreation with animal welfare, Hikes with Hounds creates a win-win: dogs enjoy a break filled with adventure and attention, and volunteers experience the reward of helping a dog shine beyond the adoption floor. Ready to join us? Register by clicking here! Learn more by emailing our team at volunteer@orangecountync.gov .

(if needed, we can provide a printed PDF upon request) Check out the animals needing rescue most by viewing the pet listing here! Read the Placement Partner Guidelines If you are a 501(c)(3) rescue group and are interested in becoming an OCAS Placement Partner, submit a completed Placement Partner Profile, Placement Partner Agreement and a copy of your organization’s 501c3 to Animal Services: By email: adoption@orangecountync.gov By fax: 919-918-2393 By mail to Orange County Animal Services, 1601 Eubanks Road, Chapel Hill, NC 27516 WORKING WITH US Communication Disease Prevention & Control Guidance & Regulations No Cost Medical Services Sterilization & Microchips WORKING WITH US Click on each section below for more information! Communication When a Placement Partner chooses to work with OCAS, we want to ensure that the partnership is one that lasts and that there are no surprises. Therefore, we partner under a specialized set of guidelines that have been developed to specifically address the needs and expectations of both OCAS and our Partner Organizations. We also ensure that every dog or cat a Partner Organizations receives comes with a full medical record, temperament record and memorandum of any special circumstances or additional treatments it may need in the future. Orange County Animal Services aims to provide a mutually beneficial program to all of our Placement Partners. We achieve this through our strict standards of care and by working with our partner organizations to place as many sound animals as possible. We strive to make it easier for our placement partners to continue to offer their services to the people and animals of Orange County and beyond. Disease Prevention & Control Disease prevention is one of our most serious concerns at OCAS. All animals that enter our Shelter Division are given a medical examination upon intake to screen for disease. Additionally, animals are given standard vaccinations. Guidance & Regulations Domestic companion animals must be moved to the state of destination in accordance with that state's laws. No Cost Medical Services All cats and dogs receive the following standard services at no cost to Placement Partner Organizations: Bordatella vaccination (dogs and puppies three weeks and older) Deworming DHPP vaccination (dogs and puppies six weeks and older) Flea/Tick Treatment FVRCP vaccination (cats and kittens six weeks and older) Heartworm preventative Heartworm test (antigen test; dogs six months and older) Physical exam Rabies vaccination (if older than three months of age) In addition to these standard services, all animals are given a basic evaluation to screen for aggression, and most dogs are given a more in-depth behavioral evaluation during their stay with us. Sterilization & Microchips We offer discounted sterilization performed by licensed and experienced veterinarians. We are also able to provide microchip implantation to cats or dogs before they are transferred to a rescue organization. These optional services offer huge savings and convenience for our partnering organizations, and are available for the following rates: Microchipping - $35 Neuters (dogs and cats!) - $30 Spays (dogs and cats!) - $60

Website Sign In Home Government Departments G - Z Health Department Community Health Assessment Community Health Assessment What is a Community Health Assessment? Every four years, Orange County completes a Community Health Assessment (CHA). This process seeks to understand the overall health of Orange County and identify what matters most for the health of the county. The CHA uses data from surveys, interviews, and other feedback from partners and community members and data from outside sources like the NC State Center for Health Statistics and the U.S. Census data. This data and feedback is used to set community health priorities and develop Community Health Improvement Plans (CHIPs). Healthy Carolinians of Orange County leads the CHA process and works with residents, civic groups, nonprofits, schools, health care providers, and other partners. Community Health Improvement Plans and State of the County Health Reports Community Health Improvement Plans (CHIPs) are developed after the formal CHA document is complete. The CHIPs identify goals for each priority and include projects and actions to meet the goals. For the years between CHA documents, the Health Department produces a State of the County Health (SOTCH) report to share updates, emerging concerns, and new initiatives conducted in the year before. Current documents 2023 Orange County Community Health Assessment Community Health Improvement Plans are available on this online platform . 2024 State of the County Health Report (opens in a new window). 2025 State of the County Health Report . Website Sign In Home Government Departments G - Z Health Department Healthy Homes Healthy Homes Program About the program If you live in Orange County and want to make your home healthier and safer, the Orange County Health Department’s Healthy Homes program can help. Healthy Homes is free and teaches families how to reduce health and safety risks at home. A Healthy Homes Environmental Health Specialist can help you find and fix common problems like: Poor air quality (including asthma triggers) Fire safety risks Fall hazards Household poisoning risks Safer gun storage Private well/onsite water safety Childhood lead exposure What to expect A Healthy Homes Environmental Health Specialist will schedule a home assessment . During the visit, they look for environmental issues that could be making people sick or causing injuries. After the visit, you’ll get a report with steps to make your home safer and healthier. During the home assessment, we will: I dentify possible health and safety hazards in the home Share practical tips for home safety and environmental health Provide education on green cleaning and safer cleaning choices Connect you with affordable housing resources when available Offer follow-up support when needed Healthy Homes serves people who: Live in Orange County Scheduling an assessment Self-referral Contact Healthy Homes staff: Email: jaguilar@orangecountync.gov Phone: 919-245-2368 Self-assessment tool You may be able to start with a self-assessment tool (ask staff for details). Medical provider referrals Medical providers can refer a child who lives in Orange County and has poorly controlled asthma using the provider referral form upon request. Language Assistance Interpretation and translation services are available upon request. Servicios de interpretación y traducción son ofrecidos con su solicitud. What's new in Healthy Homes? Preventing accidental poisonings in your home. To children, lots of medicines look just like candy. Store medicines safely: up, away, and locked. Find a spot in your home that is too high for kids to reach or see . Every home is different—pick the safest place for yours. Walk around your home and choose the best spot to store: Medicines (prescription and over-the-counter) Vitamins Supplements Gummy products , including CBD gummies Keep these items up and away—every time , even between doses. Don’t forget what you carry with you Medicines and supplements that travel with you should also be out of sight and out of reach , including items in: Purses and bags Pockets Backpacks Pill organizers Need help? Contact Orange County Health Department (OCHD) if you: Need help finding a safe storage spot, or Need a locking box for medicines and supplements.
